newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends stronger on bullish sentiment.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends stronger on bullish sentiment.

text.p: The won continued to climb higher versus the dollar on Thursday as the general market sentiment turned to its favour, traders said.
Wide-spread expectation that the government will support the domestic currency if it falls near the 830 won level lured buyers away from buying dollars, they said.
The won closed at 826.20 after opening at an intraday low of 827.50. It touched a high of 826.00.
Traders said the market was relatively quiet in thin trading.
"The dollar is going through a downward correction after sharp rises last week," said a dealer at a domestic bank.
Tight won liquidity in the money market also prevented banks from buying dollars.
Dealers said the won's movement on Friday would depend heavily on the size of imports.
A range of 826.00 to 828.00 is forecast for Friday with a base mid-rate of 826.60. Today's mid-rate stood at 828.10.
